attempted_claim: Let (X,omega) be the monotone 4-point blowup X=Bl_4 CP^2 over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 5. Let C=F(X)_{lambda,Q} be a toroidal subcategory in the sense of Smith (Definition 1.6): a summand of the split-closed monotone Fukaya category split-generated by a monotone Lagrangian torus equipped with an isolated critical point of its superpotential. If T_1=(L_1,xi_1) and T_2=(L_2,xi_2) are two toroidal generators of the same C — two monotone Lagrangian tori with isolated critical local systems whose localized closed-open maps define the same factor Q in QH^*(X) — are T_1 and T_2 quasi-isomorphic up to shift? In particular, does Smith's stable equivalence T_1^{oplus 2} + T_1[1]^{oplus 2} ≃ T_2^{oplus 2} + T_2[1]^{oplus 2} upgrade to T_1 ≃ T_2 or T_1 ≃ T_2[1]?
decisive_failure: correctness: Computations verify: affine zeros (0,4),(3,3),(4,0),(4,4); torus Hessians [[3,2],[2,3]] det0 rank1 and [[0,4],[4,0]] det4 Morse; local lengths 1 at (4,4) via independent linears and 2 at (3,3) via K unit plus diagonal (x-3)^2(x-4); Clifford idempotents 2 vs 4 reproduce. But essential categorical inferences fail: (1) Krull-Schmidt claimed via false 'finite global dimension' for k[v]/(v^2) plus unproved K0-rank/idempotent-lift, not the correct Hom-finite Karoubian theorem; (2) C2 Perf(k)xPerf(k) HF-dim argument numerically inconsistent (a^2+b^2=4 admits no both-factor solution; S1+S2 total 2 not 4) and Perf solution list unlinked to classification; (3) universal quantifier over all toroidal C reduced without proof to two summands from one W, with no Hessian-rank or QH* argument covering other tori. Hence upgrade not established.

record_title: Toroidal-generator uniqueness up to shift in a fixed monotone del Pezzo surface
recovery_conditions: repair the decisive proof or computational defect and recheck the full claim; introduce a materially new method or a justified, still-valuable revised claim; address the recorded limitation: Invokes (not re-proves) Smith Theorems C/D/E, Dyckerhoff smoothness and split-generation, and the HF*=Clifford(Hessian) identification via the Oh spectral sequence; Krull-Schmidt is justified via Hom-finiteness, split-closedness, finite decomposition, and local endomorphism rings of indecomposables. No claim beyond Bl_4 CP^2 in characteristic 5; non-isolated critical points never generate toroidal subcategories.
